title: Use POSIT_PLATFORM secrets for app token
description:
## Summary

Replace the generic `APP_ID` / `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets with the app-specific
`POSIT_PLATFORM_APP_ID` / `POSIT_PLATFORM_PEM` secrets provisioned by
[rstudio/github-iac](https://github.com/rstudio/github-iac).

The `posit-platform` GitHub App is already installed on this repo and its
credentials are already shared with it via the Pulumi config, so this is a
drop-in rename with no infrastructure changes required.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger the issue automation workflow (open a test issue) and confirm
      the run still succeeds
- [ ] Confirm the bot actor on the resulting label / project-add events is
      still `posit-platform[bot]`

title: Fix builds on macOS
description:
This fixes a few compatibility cases and allows the project to be built on macOS:

* Define `HOST_NAME_MAX` to its POSIX equivalent if not present.

* Gate calls to `ptrctl()`, which is a Linux-specific syscall.

* Include `<signal.h>`, which is the canonical header for `kill()`.

* Use C++17, which is required for our use of `weak_for_this()` when building with Clang.

macOS builds are useful for testing with the smoke-test tool; obviously the Launcher itself does not run on macOS.

title: Fix issues with cleaning up tail processes and wait for output files to be created
description:
This PR fixes a number of issues with cleaning up the `tail` subprocesses that are launched by the `FileOuputStream` class:

* A lack of permission to kill the child processes (fixed in `system/Process.cpp`)
* A deadlock when a job is killed while the output stream is open (fixed using `std::recursive_mutex` because the issue was locking the same mutex on one thread, and it's simpler than trying to enforce that developers never invoke an operation that locks that mutex from within the status update callback)
* An issue where streams were never cancelled (in some circumstances) because they were never flagged as started)

This PR also implements support for waiting for output files to be created before attempting to read them, based on the implementation in the IDE.

Fixes #22.

title: Fix an issue with pruning jobs
description:
There was a structural flaw in pruning jobs on startup. The job repository would get initialized during plugin start up, which would initialize the job pruner. Then, during bootstrap, the list of existing jobs would get populated via a call to `IJobSource::getJobs` and the SDK would add each job to the repository. Because the job pruner is relying on the job status notifier to notify it of job updates, and these jobs are being added directly to the repository (bypassing the job status notifier), pruning would never get triggered. To resolve this I refactored in the following way:

* `IJobSource::getJobs` pure virtual method becomes the pure virtual method `JobRepository::loadJobs`. 
* TODO #8 is moved into `QuickStartJobRepository::loadJobs`.
* `JobRepository` is renamed to `AbstractJobRepository` to reflect its incompleteness in its name.
* `AbstractJobRepository::onJobAdded` virtual method is added to allow the Plugin to perform custom actions when a job is newly added to the repository
* `LocalJobStorage` is renamed `LocalJobRepostiory` and now extends from `AbstractJobRepository`. It no longer subscribes to all jobs itself - it relies on `AbstractJobRepository` to watch for new jobs.

The TODO #8 documentation and example in the QuickStart guide was updated to reflect the refactoring. I also added an advanced feature section for the methods `AbstractJobRepository::onJobAdded`, `AbstractJobRepository::onJobRemoved`, and `AbstractJobRepository::onInitialize`.

This PR also fixes a bug where the `AllJobStatusStream` never actually subscribed to the `JobStatusNotifier`. After this PR, it is possible to launch R Sessions through the sample Local plugin.

title: Add support for GET /info and /clusters
description:
This PR adds support for getting cluster info through the optional overriding of several capabilities-reporting methods on IJobSource.

It also updates the examples in QuickStart to use different classes of "things" for the name of the example organization and the name of the example job scheduling system. I also tried to be more consistent in providing code samples.

One thing I debated about for this feature was whether it would be better to have several methods for reporting capabilities, or create a `Capabilites` struct and have one method that is responsible for correctly populating that struct. I eventually picked the several methods style, but I'm still torn about it and interested to hear feedback.

It also adds generating these documents to the Jenkins job.

Neither guide is complete. Ideally, from this point on, the guides will be updated with relevant sections as I finish features in the SDK.

title: Set up the cmake project and the basic folder structure.
description:
This PR adds the CMake project for the SDK, the Singularity plugin and the QuickStart Plugin. The QuickStart Plugin has the first two TODOs (rename the namespaces as desired, e.g. rstudio -> myorg, quickstart -> gridengine), and rename all QuickStart* classes as desired (e.g. QuickStartMain -> GridEngineMain).

It also adds the dependency on boost, and a small helper script that can be used to install boost in the default install location. I decided to go with the default install location and default installation of boost because we won't ship boost with the SDK. Users of the SDK can clone the Git repository and compile the project with CMake, or download a source package and compile from source that way. Either way, they will need to install the 3rd party dependencies independently.

The license hasn't been decided on yet (as far as I can recall), so I left it as a TODO in the header comments.
